narrative:
The prediction estimated an 86% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, so your loan was denied. This does not mean repayment is certain to fail; it means your application closely resembles past borrowers who struggled, so the bank declined the risk.

The strongest reason was your checking account status: it was overdrawn below zero, a condition seen in only about 12.6% of approved applicants. That pushed the decision most strongly toward bad risk. The second most important factor was your credit history: although it shows all credits at this bank were paid, this pattern is very rare among approved applicants—only 2.9%—and, alongside your current account position, it did not reassure the prediction. It also leaned toward bad risk. Third, your property status was recorded as unknown or none, while most approved applicants have a car, real estate, or a building-society/life-insurance asset. That lack of recorded collateral also pushed toward denial.

Your requested amount, 1,442 DM, was below the approved average, and your 18-month term was close to average, but these positives were not enough to overcome the top concerns.

Next, bring your checking account into positive standing, avoid missed payments, and build a more conventional credit record. Provide proof of assets or collateral, consider adding a creditworthy guarantor, reduce existing debts if possible, and ask the bank for a manual review or specific steps before reapplying.
